prose.title: The Champ Won on Offense. Eric Martel Won the Game. Boo-yah.
prose.dek: The forecast's favorite scored ninth, the man who paid the auction's top price for Josh Allen did not win a game, and the guy who runs this website swept his division while starting a quarterback who went backwards.

desk.speaker: stuart
desk.text: Welcome to UPS Center, everybody. Week one is in the books, and before anybody gets comfortable I have to drop some knowledge. The preseason forecast told you Bear Dunn was {{f.pre.0009.power_rank}}. Then the games started, and Bear Dunn posted {{f.team.0009.week_points_rank}}. Rich?

desk.speaker: rich
desk.text: Thanks, Stu. Meanwhile the man ranked {{f.pre.0005.power_rank}}, the team the preview called stacked everywhere but quarterback, went {{f.team.0005.week_allplay}} against the field. Eric Martel, {{f.team.0005.score}}, {{f.team.0005.week_points_rank}}. He GOT it.

desk.speaker: stuart
desk.text: And check the record book, Rich: that's {{f.wire.record_team_score}}. The game itself, against Cutting, is {{f.wire.record_combined_game}}. And his best receiver barely showed up! {{f.week.bust_1}}. Did not matter one bit. {{f.team.0005.boom}}. Cool as the other side of the pillow.

desk.speaker: rich
desk.text: But look where the rest of it came from, Stu. {{f.team.0005.idp_pts}} points from his defenders, {{f.team.0005.idp_rank}}. T.J. Watt alone: {{f.star.idp.line}}, good for {{f.star.idp.score}}. Did you know? Brian Cutting, the defending champion, put up {{f.team.0004.off_rank}} and still lost to him. Shawn Blake had a scouting report on that defense Sunday night.

desk.speaker: stuart
desk.text: Fluky, Shawn? The champ won the offense and lost the game, and Martel's defenders more than doubled his. Quentin Lake chipped in {{f.player.quentin-lake.score}} from the secondary. See, what had happened was, the other team brought defenders. Rich!

desk.speaker: rich
desk.text: Let's check the rest of the forecast's homework. Bear Dunn came in with {{f.pre.0009.sim_p_title}} title odds, the best in the league. He went {{f.team.0009.week_allplay}} against the field. And the best pickup of the week, {{f.wire.best_add}}, was Bear Dunn's. He scored every one of those points on Bear's bench.

desk.speaker: stuart
desk.text: Now, the projections backed his lineup calls, so this is not a bad call, this is a bad Sunday. He still left {{f.team.0009.left_on_bench}} points on that bench, and he {{f.team.0009.could_have_won}}. Rich, you have to do the next one. I cannot.

desk.speaker: rich
desk.text: In the interest of full disclosure, Stu: the man who runs this website. Keith Creelman spent more than anyone at the auction, and one of the things he bought was Kyler Murray. Week one: {{f.team.0008.bust}}.

desk.speaker: stuart
desk.text: Negative! The man went backwards! And on the bench, the insurance policy he bought at that same auction. {{f.team.0008.bench_miss}}. The projections going in: {{f.team.0008.bench_proj}}. That is not bad luck, that is a bad call. Can I get a witness from the congregation?

desk.speaker: rich
desk.text: Witness here, and the congregation says guilty. He won both games anyway, and against Josh Martel he can thank a receiver: {{f.team.0008.boom}}. The site owner leaned on Christian Watson, and yes, Keith, it is in the recap. It is in the recap right now.

desk.speaker: stuart
desk.text: Now the best line in the league. Caleb Williams: {{f.star.line}}. {{f.star.score}} points for Josh Martel. He must be the bus driver, because he was taking the Carolina defense to school.

desk.speaker: rich
desk.text: And the biggest bargain belonged to a man who lost twice. {{f.bb.off.bargain.1}}. Bousquet got Coker from Matt Gerardi in the Amon-Ra St. Brown trade.

desk.speaker: stuart
desk.text: And the bust list starts right where we started, Rich: {{f.bb.off.bust.1}}. Next up, {{f.bb.off.bust.2}}. On defense, the bargain: {{f.bb.idp.bargain.1}}. The bust: {{f.bb.idp.bust.1}}.

desk.speaker: rich
desk.text: Five of each, offense and defense, every one measured against MFL's last projection before that player's kickoff.

desk.speaker: stuart
desk.text: Now separate bad luck from bad usage, Rich. Expected fantasy points take every target, carry and throw, where it happened on the field, and ask what that usage normally scores in our league. Ja'Marr Chase had {{f.bb.off.bust.1.xfp}}. Drake London: {{f.bb.off.bust.2.xfp}}. That is not a cold day. That is no looks.

desk.speaker: rich
desk.text: And Kenneth Walker III went the other way, Stu. MFL had him in the bargain bin, and his usage was {{f.bb.off.bargain.2.xfp}}. The role was real. Furthest over expected in the league: {{f.xfp.over.1}}. Furthest under: {{f.xfp.under.1}}.

desk.speaker: stuart
desk.text: Burrow had the volume and Bear Dunn got the leftovers. That is a bad beat, not a bad call. Let's go to the divisions.

captions.t.offidp: The defending champion scored the most on offense. The league's best score came from the man who scored the most on defense.
captions.t.pickups: The two best adds of the week never made a lineup. Four of the five adds that did belong to the owner who benched his own insurance.
captions.t.performers: Two quarterbacks up top in a superflex league, and a Kansas City running back crashing the party.

desk.speaker: stuart
desk.text: Four divisions, every game a division game this week. In every division, somebody went two-and-oh and somebody went oh-and-two. The division of the week is Outlast PG Time, {{f.pot.outlast-pg-time.pre_strength}}, and it delivered {{f.pot.outlast-pg-time.points_rank}}. Rich?

desk.speaker: rich
desk.text: And here is the stat of the week, Stu. Of the four preseason division favorites, exactly one won both of his games, and he plays in Maddie Mondays. The other three went a combined two-and-four.

p.1.speaker: stuart
p.1.text: Outlast PG Time came in {{f.pot.outlast-pg-time.pre_strength}}, with {{f.pot.outlast-pg-time.pre_title_odds}} of the title odds between three teams. Eric Martel went {{f.team.0005.pot_record}} in here and it was not close. Doing it, doing it, doing it well.

p.1.speaker: rich
p.1.text: Eric Martel beat the defending champ, Brian Cutting, by {{f.game.02.margin}} -- and it wasn't close enough for lineup decisions to matter, {{f.game.02.ceiling}}. For the record, {{f.game.02.upset}}. Cutting actually won the offensive scoreboard; Martel's defense is what buried him.

p.1.speaker: stuart
p.1.text: Cutting did get one back, Brian Cross by {{f.game.03.margin}}, and {{f.team.0004.boom}}. Ashton Jeanty breaks off something proper.

p.1.speaker: rich
p.1.text: Which leaves Brian Cross, Stu. Got paid to take a quarterback, spent the summer on defense, and the forecast gave him {{f.pre.0006.idp_proj_rank}}. That defense posted {{f.team.0006.idp_rank}}. His quarterbacks were fine, {{f.team.0006.boom}}. Didn't matter: Eric Martel beat him by {{f.game.01.margin}} -- the largest margin in the league this week -- and Brian Cutting beat him by {{f.game.03.margin}}. Same verdict both times: {{f.team.0006.could_have_won}}.

p.1.speaker: stuart
p.1.text: And Cross was antsy one game into the season, Rich. A.J. Brown went down in the NFL opener on Wednesday night, and first thing Thursday morning Cross was in the Coffee Shop.

p.1.speaker: rich
p.1.text: He had reason to sweat, Stu. The forecast took note -- {{f.live.0006.injury_note}}. His playoff odds are down to {{f.live.0006.current_playoff_odds}}, from {{f.pre.0006.sim_p_playoffs}} before the season.

p.2.speaker: rich
p.2.text: The forecast came back with Bear Dunn's name on top, Stu. {{f.pre.0009.power_rank}}, with {{f.pre.0009.off_proj_rank}} and {{f.pre.0009.idp_proj_rank}}. Eric Mannila, {{f.pre.0011.power_rank}}, beat him by {{f.game.05.margin}}. For the record, {{f.game.05.upset}}.

p.2.speaker: stuart
p.2.text: Not everybody bought that forecast, Rich. The preview gave Bear Dunn a {{f.pre.0009.sim_p_last}} chance to finish last, and on Sunday night Ryan Bousquet quoted it back to the Coffee Shop with a review of his own.

p.2.speaker: rich
p.2.text: Poppycock, he says. One week in, the model is not backing down: Bear Dunn's playoff odds are {{f.live.0009.current_playoff_odds}}, the best in the league.

p.2.speaker: stuart
p.2.text: The forecast called Mannila the one that looks wrong: the third-most valuable offense in the league, ranked {{f.pre.0011.power_rank}}. Week one leaned his way: {{f.team.0011.pot_record}} in the division, and Jaxson Dart put up {{f.player.jaxson-dart.score}}. He did it with {{f.team.0011.week_points_rank}}, which is how you sweep the division with {{f.pot.dog-pound-4-life.points_rank}}. Holla at a playa when you see him in the street!

p.2.speaker: rich
p.2.text: And against Mannila, {{f.game.05.ceiling}}. The projections backed Dunn's lineup, the points just landed on the bench, {{f.team.0009.left_on_bench}} of them, and the best pickup of the week was one of the men sitting there. He did take the other game, over Chris Klingenberg by {{f.game.06.margin}}.

p.2.speaker: stuart
p.2.text: Which brings us to Chris Klingenberg, with {{f.team.0012.week_points_rank}}. Also the fewest on offense. Also the fewest on defense. {{f.team.0012.week_allplay}} against the field. It was one week, Chris.

p.3.speaker: stuart
p.3.text: Maddie Mondays, the division the forecast called the tightest in the league. The preview said Keith Creelman led it on paper. Week one he went {{f.team.0008.pot_record}} and leads it on the field. Rich, I am contractually obligated to say something nice.

p.3.speaker: rich
p.3.text: Nice is not the word, Stu. He started Kyler Murray over his own insurance policy and beat Josh Martel by {{f.game.08.margin}} anyway. Christian Watson covered for him with {{f.player.christian-watson.score}}, and Watson gets the first fruit cup.

p.3.speaker: stuart
p.3.text: Josh Martel had the best player in the entire league, Caleb Williams, {{f.player.caleb-williams.score}}, and his defense posted {{f.team.0007.idp_rank}}. He still went {{f.team.0007.pot_record}}, and against Creelman {{f.game.08.ceiling}}.

p.3.speaker: rich
p.3.text: And the rest of that offense, Stu? Josh Martel did the math himself on Tuesday morning.

p.3.speaker: stuart
p.3.text: He does not wanna talk about it, Rich. Unfortunately for Josh, this is a recap show.

p.3.speaker: rich
p.3.text: And Ryan Bousquet, {{f.pre.0001.power_rank}} coming in. Jalen Coker handed him the biggest surprise of the week, and his quarterbacks handed a lot of it back. He went {{f.team.0001.pot_record}}, and his best possible lineup was {{f.team.0001.ceiling_rank}}. No perfect card was saving this one, Stu. And he saw it coming before the late games were over on Sunday.

p.3.speaker: stuart
p.3.text: Called his shot, Rich. Not the shot you want to call, but he called it.

p.4.speaker: stuart
p.4.text: LEGION OF BOOM! The forecast had it {{f.pot.legion-of-boom.pre_strength}}. Derrick Whitman built this division as a captain, and in July he picked Shawn Blake to win it. Week one, Whitman went {{f.team.0002.pot_record}}, and one of those wins came over Shawn Blake. Boo-yah!

p.4.speaker: rich
p.4.text: Blake paid the auction's top price for Josh Allen, Stu, and Allen delivered: {{f.team.0010.boom}}. Blake went {{f.team.0010.pot_record}} anyway. {{f.team.0010.bust}}, and Blake {{f.team.0010.could_have_won}}. Allen did his job. The receivers did not get the memo.

p.4.speaker: stuart
p.4.text: And Blake knew it by Sunday night, Rich. Oh-and-two, and he opened for business.

p.4.speaker: rich
p.4.text: One week into a fourteen-week season, Stu. Brian Cross told him it was only week one a minute earlier. Blake was not hearing it.

p.4.speaker: stuart
p.4.text: And here comes {{f.pre.0003.power_rank}} Matt Gerardi. For the record, {{f.game.12.upset}}. The team the forecast gave {{f.pre.0003.off_proj_rank}} posted {{f.team.0003.off_rank}}. Can I get a witness?

p.4.speaker: rich
p.4.text: Hold the witness, Stu. {{f.team.0003.bench_miss}}, and against Whitman {{f.team.0003.bench_flip}}. The Coffee Shop noticed while it was happening. Josh Martel, Sunday afternoon.

p.4.speaker: stuart
p.4.text: Sprung! But was it the wrong call? On the evidence we have, {{f.team.0003.bench_verdict}}.

p.4.speaker: rich
p.4.text: His top starter was {{f.team.0003.best_player}}, the receiver who came over in the trade that sent Darnold and Coker to Bousquet.

captions.t.burns: The two biggest same-position bench swings of the week. Both owners started the lower-projected quarterback, and only one of them runs this website.

desk.speaker: stuart
desk.text: Four divisions, four leaders, every one of them two-and-oh: {{f.div.outlast-pg-time.leader}}, {{f.div.dog-pound-4-life.leader}}, {{f.div.maddie-mondays.leader}} and {{f.div.legion-of-boom.leader}}. Rich, check the forecast.

desk.speaker: rich
desk.text: The top three in the preseason rankings were Bear Dunn, Brian Cutting and Shawn Blake. None of them won both games. Blake did not win one. The owners ranked fourth, fifth, seventh and eighth all went two-and-oh.

desk.speaker: stuart
desk.text: And the bottom of the board? {{f.pre.0003.power_rank}} Matt Gerardi posted {{f.team.0003.week_points_rank}}. The forecast gave him {{f.pre.0003.sim_p_title}} to win the whole thing, and he just beat Shawn Blake. Better recognize.

desk.speaker: rich
desk.text: Easy, Stu. It is one week of a long season, and one week is a data point, not a verdict. Bear Dunn had a winning lineup on his bench, and nobody in this league should be writing him off after one Sunday.

desk.speaker: stuart
desk.text: Then explain Bear Dunn to me, Rich. {{f.team.0009.week_allplay}} against the field, and his playoff odds went up.

desk.speaker: rich
desk.text: One week is one week, Stu. Since the preseason the projections changed, injuries hit, and the whole league shifted around him -- and Dunn's roster came out of it projecting better than anybody's. He sits at {{f.pv.sit.0009}}.

desk.speaker: stuart
desk.text: So here is where everybody sits, Rich. Up top: {{f.pv.sit.top}}. At the bottom: {{f.pv.sit.bottom}}.

desk.speaker: rich
desk.text: Biggest climbers since the preseason: {{f.pv.sit.risers}}. Biggest drops: {{f.pv.sit.fallers}}.

desk.speaker: stuart
desk.text: Nobody climbed more than Eric Martel, and he went {{f.team.0005.week_allplay}} against the field. It's your world, kid. The rest of us are still paying rent. Rich, take us home.

desk.speaker: rich
desk.text: Chris Klingenberg, week two is a fresh card. Keith, bench the negative quarterback. Stu, take us to week two.

bullets: The desk is written in tribute to Stuart Scott and Rich Eisen and their years together on the SportsCenter set. The catchphrases are theirs; everything else on the desk is ours.

captions.t.preseason: The preseason order against one week of football. Read it for fun, not for betting.
captions.t.standings: Eric Mannila is two-and-oh with a losing all-play record. Division winners take the top two seeds; all-play orders everybody else.

desk.speaker: stuart
desk.text: Thursday means Elias, Rich. The official stat changes for week one were published {{f.elias.published}}: {{f.elias.summary}}.

desk.speaker: rich
desk.text: The scoreboard moved a little, Stu: {{f.elias.teams}}. The biggest single change: {{f.elias.biggest}}. Every result stands, and so does every all-play record. The rest of the show keeps the numbers as we first published them; the corrected scores are right here.

desk.speaker: stuart
desk.text: Now week two, Rich. Every number in this segment is as of {{f.pv.cutoff}}, and injury news will move them before Sunday. And {{f.pv.division_games}}, so every result this week crosses a division line.

desk.speaker: rich
desk.text: The biggest swing on the board is {{f.pv.g1.matchup}}. The model makes {{f.pv.g1.favorite}} a {{f.pv.g1.fav_chance}} favorite, which is a coin flip in a nice suit. {{f.pv.g1.fav_stakes}}; {{f.pv.g1.dog_stakes}}. But it is not that black and white, Stu: {{f.pv.g1.fav_nuance}}. The upset path: {{f.pv.g1.upset_path}}. The flip factor: {{f.pv.g1.flip}}. And the history: {{f.pv.g1.h2h}}.

desk.speaker: stuart
desk.text: Then {{f.pv.g2.matchup}}. {{f.pv.g2.favorite}} is {{f.pv.g2.fav_chance}} to win it. {{f.pv.g2.fav_stakes}}; {{f.pv.g2.dog_stakes}}. And {{f.pv.g2.fav_same_score}}, {{f.pv.g2.dog_same_score}}. The upset path? {{f.pv.g2.upset_path}}. The flip factor: {{f.pv.g2.flip}}. The history: {{f.pv.g2.h2h}}.

desk.speaker: rich
desk.text: And {{f.pv.g3.matchup}}, with Brian Cross already oh-and-two. {{f.pv.g3.favorite}} is {{f.pv.g3.fav_chance}} to win it. {{f.pv.g3.fav_stakes}}; {{f.pv.g3.dog_stakes}}. And {{f.pv.g3.fav_same_score}}, {{f.pv.g3.dog_same_score}}. The upset path: {{f.pv.g3.upset_path}}. The flip factor: {{f.pv.g3.flip}}. The history: {{f.pv.g3.h2h}}.

desk.speaker: stuart
desk.text: Division watch, Rich. {{f.pv.div.outlast-pg-time.line}}.

desk.speaker: rich
desk.text: {{f.pv.div.dog-pound-4-life.line}}. Yes, the man at one-and-one is the favorite over the man at two-and-oh. The projections still like Bear Dunn.

desk.speaker: stuart
desk.text: {{f.pv.div.maddie-mondays.line}}. And {{f.pv.div.legion-of-boom.line}}.

desk.speaker: rich
desk.text: Injury watch. {{f.pv.inj.count}} carry a Questionable or Doubtful tag on MFL as of the cutoff. The one that costs the most if he sits: {{f.pv.inj.top}}.

desk.speaker: stuart
desk.text: And remember, Rich: a Questionable tag can turn into a start or a scratch, and every number here moves with it. We check how these calls did after week two.

desk.speaker: rich
desk.text: That is the show. For Stu, I'm Rich, and this was UPS Center. Catch you all next week.

t.pv.games.title: The six week-two matchups with the most at stake
